title: CloudSlasher — AI Multi-Cloud FinOps & Automated Cost Remediation
excerpt: Slash cloud infrastructure spend by 30-65% across OCI, AWS, Azure, GCP & Kubernetes. 100% non-invasive, zero-agent, and read-only with verified Terraform code exports.
content_html:
Slash cloud infrastructure spend by 30% to 65% across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Kubernetes clusters.

100% Non-Invasive, Read-Only IAM Credentials, Zero-Persistence Ephemeral Architecture, and Tested GitOps Terraform PRs.

How CloudSlasher Works: 5-Stage Deterministic Safety Pipeline

  1. Non-Invasive Tenancy Ingestion: Zero-agent, read-only IAM scan maps running topology across compute instances, storage volumes, databases, and network gateways.
  2. FOCUS 1.0 Lakehouse Analytics: Normalizes billing records with sub-25ms vectorized DuckDB queries to identify idle and oversized resources.
  3. Interactive What-If Modeling: Compound multi-vector cost simulator reveals immediate and 12-month runway savings.
  4. Targeted Terraform Synthesizer: Generates declarative, reviewable HCL patches with automatic companion rollback modules.
  5. 1-Click GitOps Pull Request: Dispatches non-destructive PRs to your GitHub repository with zero direct-write access to production main branches.

How CloudSlasher Compares with Infracost and Auto-Delete Tools

  • CloudSlasher vs. Infracost: Infracost operates shift-left inside CI/CD to estimate proposed cost diffs on pull requests. CloudSlasher operates post-deployment on live fleets to discover active waste that was already provisioned. They complement each other: Infracost guards your pipeline, while CloudSlasher continuously remediates live estate waste.
  • CloudSlasher vs. CAST AI / Finout: Many tools require intrusive daemon agents and execute automated terminations that can cause production outages. CloudSlasher is 100% non-invasive, uses zero persistent credentials, and exports reviewable Terraform pull requests with safety branches and companion rollbacks.
